ask.a1_html: The Quran places sabr among the believer's defining qualities and promises the patient a reward without measure Quran 39:10. When the heart contracts, He reminds us that He is with the patient Quran 2:153, and that ease follows every hardship Quran 94:5. The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to bear "a beautiful patience" Quran 70:5 — without complaint to creation.

c1.d: "In the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest." A collection for when the chest tightens.

c10.d: "Allah is enough for us — and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

c11.d: Those who restrain their anger — Allah loves them.

c12.d: The hearts of the believers tremble at the remembrance of Allah.

c13.d: The du'a of Ayyub ﷺ: "Hardship has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful."

c14.d: "Indeed, to Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return."
c14.t: When you lose a loved one

c15.d: "My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small."

c16.d: The du'a of Zakariyya ﷺ: "Grant me from Yourself a goodly offspring."

c17.d: "Whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out for him."

c18.d: Doubt becomes dangerous when you keep silent about it.

c19.d: "Glory be to Him who subjected this to us."

c2.d: Sabr is holding the heart back from complaint. Allah is with the patient.

c20.d: Allah will replace evil deeds with good ones.
c20.t: To walk away from a sin

c21.d: "Whoever places his trust in Allah, He is enough for him."

c22.d: "Call upon Me — I will respond to you."

c23.d: If Shaytan whispers — take refuge in Allah.

c24.d: "Let them rejoice in the mercy of Allah."

c25.d: Surah Al-Kahf — light between two Fridays.

c26.d: The month in which the Quran was revealed.

c27.d: "The Night of Qadr is better than a thousand months."

c28.d: He placed love and mercy between spouses.

c3.d: Shukr is to see a blessing and return it with the heart, the tongue, and your deeds.

c30.d: "O soul at peace — return to your Lord, well-pleased."

c4.d: No one is alone while he knows Allah is closer than the jugular vein.

c5.d: Musa's ﷺ du'a before Pharaoh — open my chest, ease my task, untie the knot.

c6.d: Ayat al-Kursi and the mu'awwidhat — what the Prophet ﷺ recited before sleep.

c7.d: To enter the day with remembrance.

c8.d: "Do not despair of the mercy of Allah."

c9.d: When grief feels endless, the Quran reminds you: it is passing.

aem.body_intro: This collection draws on the ayat that scholars, imams, and ordinary people have leaned on for centuries in moments of fear, anxiety, panic, sleeplessness, and despair. They do not treat anxiety the way medicine does — but they give you the anchor without which treatment cannot hold.
aem.scholar_quote: "Anxiety is not proof that your iman is weak. The Prophet ﷺ himself asked Allah for protection from anxiety and grief every day: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min al-hammi wa-l-hazan. This collection is not a substitute for du'a, and it is not a substitute for a doctor."
aem.disclaimer_body: If you are experiencing prolonged anxiety or thoughts of self-harm — please see a doctor. Sakeenly is not a substitute for medical care.
